title: What happens to pending litigation once a resolution plan is approved
p1: A company wins a resolution process… but what happens to all the court cases already hanging over it? Many assume those cases simply continue. The reality can be very different after a resolution plan gets approved.
p2: A common misconception is that approval only changes ownership or management. In many cases, the approved plan decides how past claims and pending disputes will be handled. Creditors and claimants may not be able to continue old battles in the same way as before.
p3: Once a resolution plan is approved under insolvency law, it becomes binding on stakeholders. This means the new owner typically gets a cleaner slate, while unresolved claims are dealt with according to the plan. The surprising part? A pending lawsuit does not always mean a future liability survives unchanged. The outcome depends on whether the claim was included and how the plan addresses it. For businesses, investors, and claimants, checking the resolution plan carefully can prevent costly surprises.
conclusion: Did you know approval of a resolution plan can change the future of pending litigation? What impact do you think this has on fairness for claimants?
